Rashi on Shabbat 128b:11:1.hebrew: אין עוקרין - רגליה לגמרי מן הארץ, דמוקצה היא לטלטלה:
Rashi on Shabbat 128b:11:1.english: One may not lift - its feet completely off the ground, because it is muktzeh [with respect] to moving it.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:11:2.hebrew: דדויי מדדינן - אוחזה בשני צדדיה בידו ומדדה, והוה טלטול טפי מדחייה שדחפה מאחריה:
Rashi on Shabbat 128b:11:2.english: We may help [it] walk - He holds it on both its sides with his hand and helps it walk, and [this] is greater handling than pushing, where he pushes it from behind.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:11:3.english: The latter clause - [That] which teaches: "One may push [it], but may not help [it] walk."

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:11:4.english: We came to [the case of] a hen - And the first clause [refers] to other birds.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:12:1.english: He should press its legs onto the ground - So that they bend, and it will not be able to brace itself upon them.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:12:2.hebrew: אי נמי לידלינהו - יגביהנו שלא יהו רגליו נוגעות לארץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 128b:12:2.english: Or alternatively, lift them - He should lift it so that its feet do not touch the ground.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:13:1.english: One may assist [it] - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:13:3.english: One may not deliver an animal on a Festival - Because there is excessive exertion.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:13:4.english: However, one may assist - it on a Festival.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:13:5.hebrew: ומיילדין אשה בשבת - ואין צריך לומר שמסעדין, וכל שכן ביום טוב:
Rashi on Shabbat 128b:13:5.english: And one may deliver a woman [in childbirth] on Shabbat - And needless to say, one may assist [her], and all the more so on a Festival.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:13:6.hebrew: וקושרין הטיבור - של ולד שהוא ארוך, שאם לא יתקשר ויכרך בשום דבר, יצאו מעיו אם יגביהו התינוק:
Rashi on Shabbat 128b:13:6.english: And one may tie the umbilical cord - Of a newborn, which is long; for if it is not tied and wrapped with something, its intestines will come out if they lift the infant.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:14:1.hebrew: דוחק - בבשר של בהמה לפנים, שיהא הולד בולט לחוץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 128b:14:1.english: Presses - on the flesh of the animal inward, so that the offspring will protrude outward.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:15:1.english: And he blows into its nostrils - For its nostrils are blocked with mucus.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:15:2.english: And he places a teat - of its mother into its mouth.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:16:1.english: Having mercy - [This means] endearing her offspring to her.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:16:2.hebrew: בול של מלח - מלא אגרוף, דכייב לה וזוכרת צער לידה, ומרחמה את הולד אם רחקתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 128b:16:2.english: A lump of salt - A fistful, since it causes her pain and she remembers the pain of childbirth, and she has mercy on the offspring if she has distanced it.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:16:3.english: Fluids of the afterbirth - They soak the afterbirth in water.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:17:1.english: Does not distance - It is not its way to distance [its offspring].

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:19:1.hebrew: מביאה לה שמן - דרך רה"ר:
Rashi on Shabbat 128b:19:1.english: [She] brings her oil - Through the public domain.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:19:2.hebrew: ביד - בכפה ולא בכלי, דכמה דאפשר משנינן:
Rashi on Shabbat 128b:19:2.english: In [her] hand - In her palm and not in a vessel, for as much as is possible we alter [the usual manner].

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:19:3.hebrew: בשערה - סכה שערה שמן, וכשבאה אצלה מקנחתו, ואין כאן חילול שבת, כיון שאין דרך הוצאה בכך:
Rashi on Shabbat 128b:19:3.english: In her hair - She anoints her hair [with] oil, and when she comes to her, she wipes it off, and there is no desecration of Shabbat here, since that is not the [normal] manner of carrying out.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:1:2.hebrew: לחתול - לא מזיק ליה ארס דנחש, שאף הנחשים היא אוכלת:
Rashi on Shabbat 128b:1:2.english: For a cat - Snake venom does not harm it, for it even eats snakes.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:1:3.english: Due to the danger - Lest a person drink from them.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:20:1.english: [It is] obvious - For saving a life overrides Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:21:1.hebrew: תיפוק ליה משום סחיטה - למה לא הביאה לה בכלי? שלא תחלל שבת בהוצאה. הכא נמי, הא קמחללה בסחיטה:
Rashi on Shabbat 128b:21:1.english: Derive [that] it [is prohibited] due to wringing - Why did she not bring [it] to her in a vessel? So that she would not desecrate Shabbat through carrying out. Here too, behold, she is desecrating [Shabbat] through wringing.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:22:1.english: There is no wringing with regard to hair - For it is hard and does not absorb [liquid].

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:22:2.english: Through her hair - She binds the vessel to her head with her hair.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:2:1.hebrew: כופין סל בפני האפרוחים - אשמעינן דכלי ניטל לדבר שאינו ניטל בשבת, ורבי יצחק משני לה בפ"ג בצריך למקומו:
Rashi on Shabbat 128b:2:1.english: One may overturn a basket in front of the chicks - [This] teaches us that a vessel may be moved for [the sake of] something that may not be moved on Shabbat, and Rabbi Yitzchak resolves it in the third chapter [as referring to a case] where one needs its place.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:3:1.english: One may help calves to walk - [One] holds [it] by its neck and sides, and pulls it and assists it, and moves its legs for it.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:3:2.hebrew: אשה מדדה את בנה - אוחזתו בזרועותיו מאחוריו ומסייעתו, והוא מניע רגליו והולך:
Rashi on Shabbat 128b:3:2.english: A woman may help her son to walk - She holds him by his arms from behind him and assists him, and he moves his feet and walks.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:3:3.hebrew: שנוטל אחת ומניח אחת - שהתינוק מניע את רגליו, כשמניח אחת מגביה אחת:
Rashi on Shabbat 128b:3:3.english: That he lifts one [foot] and places one [foot] down - That the child moves his feet: when he places one down, he lifts one.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:3:4.english: However, [if he is] dragging [his feet], it is prohibited - Because she is carrying him.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:6:1.english: And if not - For example, where the water is deep.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:7:1.hebrew: והא קמבטל כלי מהיכנו - דמשהניחם תחתיה, אין יכול לטלטלן, דדומה לסותר בנין מדרבנן:
Rashi on Shabbat 128b:7:1.english: And does he not negate a vessel's preparedness - For once he has placed them beneath it, he cannot move them, as it is similar to dismantling a structure [and is prohibited] by rabbinic law.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:7:2.hebrew: צער בעלי חיים דאורייתא - שנאמר עזוב תעזוב עמו, ואיכא מאן דדריש טעמא דקרא משום צער בעלי חיים, באלו מציאות (ב"מ דף לב:):
Rashi on Shabbat 128b:7:2.english: Causing a living creature to suffer is a Torah [law] - As it is stated: "You shall surely help [unload] with him" [Exodus 23:5], and there is one who expounds the reason for the verse [as being] because of the suffering of living creatures, in [the chapter] Eilu Metziot (Bava Metzia 32b).

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:8:1.english: Help [it] to walk, no - [Meaning] that he should not hold it by its wings while its feet touch the ground and lead it.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:9:1.hebrew: דמקפיא נפשה - מגבהת עצמה מן הארץ, ונמצא זה מטלטל. אבל אווזים, כשאוחזין בגפיהן, הן מהלכין ברגליהן. ומיהו ברה"ר לא, משום שמא יגביה מן הארץ ונמצא נושאן, דסתמא כרבנן דפליגי עליה דרבי נתן בהמצניע (לעיל שבת דף צד.), גבי המוציא חיה ועוף בין חיין בין שחוטין חייב. והאשה מדדה את בנה אפילו ברה"ר, דאי נמי מגביה ליה, חי נושא את עצמו, דהכי מוקמינן התם, דבאדם מודו רבנן לרבי נתן:
Rashi on Shabbat 128b:9:1.english: That it lifts itself - [It] raises itself from the ground, and thus this [person] ends up moving [it]. However, geese, when one holds them by their wings, they walk on their feet. Nonetheless, in a public domain [one may] not [do so], lest he lift [them] from the ground and end up carrying them; for [this] anonymous [Mishnah] accords with the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Natan in [chapter] HaMatznia (above, Shabbat 94a), regarding [the ruling that] one who carries out a wild animal or a bird, whether alive or slaughtered, is liable. And a woman may walk her son even in a public domain, for even if she lifts him, a living [creature] carries itself — for so we establish [the law] there, that with regard to a human being, the Rabbis agree with Rabbi Natan.

Rashi on Shabbat 128b:9:2.english: Lifts [itself] - Like [the expression] "Lift your hands" in Chagigah (16b).

Tosafot on Shabbat 128b:10:1.hebrew: אין עוקרין בהמה חיה ועוף - לספרים דגרסי רה"ר, הך ברייתא פליגא אקמייתא בתרתי: דדייקינן הא דדויי מדדינן אפילו ברה"ר, ולעיל קתני דווקא בחצר; ותו, סיפא דמוקמת לתרנגולת — דאין מדדין ברה"ר, ולעיל קתני דאפי' בחצר לא. ולספרים דגרסי "אין עוקרין בהמה חיה ועוף בחצר", אתי שפיר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 128b:10:1.english: One may not lift domesticated animals, non-domesticated animals, and fowl — According to the texts that read "in the public domain" [instead of "in the courtyard"], this baraita disagrees with the first [baraita] in two [respects]: [first,] that we infer [from "one may not lift... in the public domain"] that as for helping them walk, we may help them walk even in the public domain, whereas above [the baraita] teaches [that this is permitted] specifically in a courtyard; and furthermore, the latter clause [of the baraita], which you establish as referring to a hen, [implies] that one may not help [a hen] walk in the public domain, whereas above [the baraita] teaches that even in a courtyard [one may] not [help it walk]. But according to the texts that read "One may not lift domesticated animals, non-domesticated animals, and fowl in the courtyard," it works out well.

Tosafot on Shabbat 128b:1:1.hebrew: בשר תפוח מפני שהוא מאכל לחיה - תימה: לימא "מפני שהוא מאכל לכלבים"! וי"ל דכרבי יהודה אתיא, ואינו מסריח כפירוש הקונטרס, אלא חזי ליה; וכל מידי דחזי ליה לאינש לא מקצה לכלבים, אבל מפני שהוא מאכל לחיה מותר לטלטלו, דכל ישראל בני מלכים הם. ורב חסדא דלא שרי בשר תפל מהאי טעמא — לית ליה "כל ישראל בני מלכים":
Tosafot on Shabbat 128b:1:1.english: Swollen meat, because it is food for a wild beast - [This is] astonishing: let it say "because it is food for dogs"! And one can answer that it follows Rabbi Yehudah, and it is not putrefying as Rashi explained, rather it is fit for him [to eat]; and anything that is fit for a person, one does not set aside for dogs, but because it is food for a wild beast, it is permitted to move it, for all Israel are the children of kings. And Rav Chisda, who does not permit unsalted meat for this reason, does not hold [the principle that] "all Israel are the children of kings."

Tosafot on Shabbat 128b:20:1.hebrew: קמ"ל איתובי מיתבא דעתה - אע"ג דבפרק בתרא דיומא (דף פג.) אמר: חולה אין מאכילין אותו ביוה"כ אלא ע"פ מומחה, והכא שריא משום יתובי דעתא — היינו שיותר יכולה היולדת להסתכן על ידי פחד שתתפחד שמא אין עושין יפה מה שהיא צריכה, ממה שיסתכן החולה ברעב:
Tosafot on Shabbat 128b:20:1.english: It teaches us [that] her mind is settled - Even though in the last chapter of Yoma (83a) it states [that] a sick person is not fed on Yom Kippur except on the advice of an expert, whereas here it is permitted for the sake of settling [her] mind — this is because a woman in childbirth is more likely to be endangered through fear, lest she become afraid that they are not properly doing what she needs, than a sick person is to be endangered by hunger.
